title: Evaluate 30 Hz Pico control loop
goal: Prepare a bounded, operator-tested 30 Hz RLinf control-loop configuration for the single-arm Franka/Pico Release while retaining the 10 Hz baseline backup.
doneWhen: The Release configuration requests a 30 Hz Franka environment step rate and 30 Hz collection metadata rate.
Documentation states that this is an unvalidated control-rate experiment and retains the required unloaded, small-range hardware test boundary.
Focused no-hardware configuration and compatibility checks pass.
The operator receives the exact test and rollback commands.
decisions: The 10 Hz Release state is protected by local tag backup/vr-controls-20261020 before this experiment.
Set the control loop and stored dataset metadata to 30 Hz together so exported timestamps do not claim 10 Hz while samples are produced at a different requested rate.
Do not change impedance, motion scales, step guards, Desk protections, or camera configuration as part of this isolated rate experiment.
Real-hardware validation is operator-only: unloaded, small range, emergency stop reachable; stop immediately on stale motion, vibration, force, Desk warning, or error.

verification.summary: Release commit 4f713d8 requests a 30 Hz environment cadence and aligned 30 Hz collection metadata without changing other control parameters. The operator reported stable 30 Hz arm control in a live test.
checks: Hydra YAML parse confirmed step_frequency=30.0 and data_collection.fps=30
Shell syntax and Git diff whitespace checks passed
Operator-reported live test: 30 Hz arm control was stable
limitations: The requested rate is a maximum; camera, robot, and Python work may make the achieved rate lower.
The operator report confirms stable control but does not yet quantify achieved cycle frequency, camera frame freshness, or collection-data quality at 30 Hz.
